text:
julia_support: Hey team — Escalation from Acme. They see huge embedding latency spikes and unexpectedly high billing this morning. They say repeated identical inputs are sometimes missing the cache and we also saw occasional "embedding dimension mismatch" errors in the logs. Ticket: https://acme.example/t/4321 (customer redacted). Logs attached below. Can someone triage?

julia_support: snippets from the customer logs: 
```
ERROR embedding_service cache_miss id=abc123 tenant=acme request_id=zz789 model=all-embed-v2 dim_expected=1536 dim_observed=768
WARN embeddings_api latency_ms=1420 cache_hits=3 cache_misses=97 tenant=acme route=/v1/embeddings
ERROR embeddings_api dimension_mismatch request_id=zz790 expected=1536 got=768
```

nina_eng_ml: Thanks — quick questions: are they multi-tenanting behind any proxy? are they switching models or model variants mid-batch? Also, do we have the raw request example (headers/body)? The dim mismatch suggests input-to-model mapping changed (or request got proxied to a different model).

julia_support: They say they PUT requests through a sidecar that can rewrite headers. Customer provided one example curl: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Acme-Tenant: acme-prod" \
  -d '{"model":"all-embed-v2","input":["foo","bar"],"batch_size":16}'
```

omar_sre: I'm seeing correlation with bursts where our batching runtime merges small requests for efficiency. Hypothesis: batch dedupe/packing drop or normalize a header used for cache keying. If header is missing or normalized, cache namespace collapses across tenants -> cold misses + billing. Also if a request gets routed to a model with different embedding dim (e.g., embed-small vs embed-large) we could log dimension mismatches.

mike_qa: I spun a local repro for the header-mangling case. Steps: run a loop that alternates X-Tenant between "acme-a" and "acme-b" but sends all traffic through a single connection pool (simulates sidecar). Repro script: 
```
for i in {1..200}; do
  T=$((i%2));
  TENANT=$( [ $T -eq 0 ] && echo acme-a || echo acme-b );
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test" \
    -H "X-Tenant-ID: $TENANT" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"all-embed-v2","input":["same text repeated"],"batch_size":8}' &
done
wait
```
I observed ~70% cache_misses even though inputs are identical per-tenant. Metrics snapshot from the instance: 
```
metrics: {cache_hits: 28, cache_misses: 172, avg_latency_ms: 620}
cache_namespace_config: model+dim+prefix? (current code says: key = sha256(model + dim + input_prefix))
```

nina_eng_ml: That key composition is the problem: we rely on a tenant-specific namespace but the tenant header was not included in the stable hash in one codepath (batch path). Looks like a regression introduced when we added cross-request batching optimization. Root cause: batch packing omitted per-request metadata when constructing dedupe keys.

nina_eng_ml: Proposed patch: include explicit tenant id in cache key, fall back to api_key fingerprint if header absent, and assert on mixed-tenant batches (reject with 400 or force separate batches). Diff (informal): 
```
- cache_key = sha256(model + "|" + dim + "|" + input_prefix)
+ cache_key = sha256(tenant_id + "|" + model + "|" + dim + "|" + input_prefix)
+ // in batching path: if requests_in_batch contain >1 tenant_id -> split batch
```

omar_sre: Also saw a few requests where header was empty string (sidecar dropped it). For immediate mitigation we can: 1) enable per-tenant cache_namespace override at the proxy rule (customer-side), 2) enforce -X-Redwood-Tenant header required for embeddings endpoint (400 if missing) in a short-lived config. Which do we want?

julia_support: Customer wants a fast remediation — they can set the proxy to always send a deterministic header value. Can we also push a temporary guard on our side to reject mixed-tenant batches while we roll a fix?

nina_eng_ml: I'll open a PR with the patch and add a unit test that simulates mixed-tenant batch packing. Also add integration test that verifies cache_key includes tenant id. I'll mark it high-priority patch.

mike_qa: QA will validate with the repro script and add a load-run to ensure no perf regressions. Also verifying that dimension mismatch logs drop once batch-splitting is enforced.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: deploy/service=embeddings-runtime sha=deadbeef1234 env=canary region=us-west-2

deploy-bot: Canary passes (10k requests, no regressions). Rolling to 30%: deploy/service=embeddings-runtime sha=deadbeef1234 env=staged region=us-west-2

julia_support: Sent a step-by-step mitigation to Acme: 1) add stable X-Tenant-ID header, 2) if they can't edit proxy quickly, set embeddings_cache_namespace per-app in their config to a unique value (temporary), 3) expect a small rollback risk window while we put the patch in prod.

sam_acme: Thanks — we found the problem in our Envoy sidecar config: the header_tap filter we used was rewriting the header for keepalive connections. We've patched it and re-ran tests. After forcing the header we see cache_hit rate jump dramatically and billing abnormality stopped. Example from our side: 
```
Before: cache_hits=12 cache_misses=188 avg_latency=900ms
After:  cache_hits=162 cache_misses=38  avg_latency=120ms
```

omar_sre: Great. We'll keep the mixed-tenant-batch guard active for 48h and monitor for errors. Also schedule a backfill job to repopulate popular keys (best-effort) for tenants that saw cold misses.

nina_eng_ml: Added tests and a small changelog note. We'll also add a lint rule to ensure cache key composition always includes tenant_id or api_key fingerprint.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete: deploy/service=embeddings-runtime sha=deadbeef1234 env=prod region=all

julia_support: Closing loop with Acme this afternoon. Follow-ups: postmortem (owner: nina_eng_ml), add dashboard for mixed-tenant-batch rate, and update docs for embedding cache keying (customer-facing). Thanks all. :tada:

nina_eng_ml: I'll file the postmortem and link the reproducer scripts + test vectors.

mike_qa: Leaving a note to QA run a 24h soak on the fix in staging and run billing-sample checks.

julia_support: Marking resolved in support ticket and emailing customer.

sam_acme: Confirmed customer satisfied. Thanks everyone. :pray:
